title: Writing your own exception and the `Throwable` hierarchy

videos.script: Lesson 36 split exceptions into checked and unchecked. This lesson shows where that split comes from. {{tree}} Every exception and every error is a Throwable, and the branch a class sits on decides what the compiler asks of you. {{error}} One branch, Error, belongs to the JVM. A stack overflow is on it, and a catch for Exception lets it straight past. {{own}} Then an exception of your own. A member who already holds two books may not borrow a third. That deserves a name, a message and the member's id, and the compiler can make every caller deal with it. {{cause}} When you catch one exception and throw another, the first goes along as the cause, and the stack trace says Caused by. {{habits}} Last, three habits. Never swallow an exception. Add what only your code knows. And do not throw just to leave a loop. By the end, a failure in your program reaches someone who can read it.
